author: Sarah Donovan
title: Dover lower Central Ave. reconstruction raises traffic concerns - NewsBreak
text:
By Sarah Donovan Foster ,
19 hours ago DOVER — A reconstruction of lower Central Avenue, between Silver Street and Stark Avenue, is being designed now for a 2027-28 project that has some residents concerned about traffic around their homes.
The project includes replacing an existing water line which is more than a century old, updating streets and sidewalks and "reconstructing the outdated drainage collection and conveyance system," according to the city.
What to expect from reconstruction project
John Storer, the city's community services director, said they're in "the final push to try to get the design finalized so that we can proceed and go out to bid."
City engineer Jillian Semprini stated the project is "driven by the need to replace aging underground infrastructure while also improving the roadway for all users." She said the project includes "replacing a 150-year-old water main and deteriorating stormwater infrastructure" while also upgrading pedestrian, bicycle, and roadway safety.
"The project includes replacing underground utilities, including the 150-year-old water main, stormwater infrastructure, and a small portion of the sewer main," Semprini wrote in response to questions from Foster's Daily Democrat. "Surface improvements include reconstructed sidewalks, upgraded crosswalks with rectangular rapid flashing beacons, dedicated bicycle lanes where roadway width allows and shared lane markings (sharrows) elsewhere, new street trees, decorative street lighting, and full roadway reconstruction."
She said the project will also improve the Central Avenue/Stark Avenue/East Watson Street intersection.
She said bids are expected to go out this fall and be awarded in the fall or winter for construction to start in spring 2027 with completion expected in fall 2028.
Concerns raised about traffic management Allan Krans, who said he's been a resident of Renaud Avenue for 42 years, raised concerns at the city's Transportation Advisory Commission meeting July 27 about the traffic management plan for the reconstruction. Renaud Avenue is located directly off of Stark Avenue.
Krans said the neighborhood he was referring to includes Renaud Avenue, Hayes Lane, Keating Avenue, Shamrock, Birchwood and Emmet, six streets all to the west of Stark Avenue. Krans said they don't want a detour through Renaud Avenue, Shamrock Lane or Birchwood Place.
"Even if we all agree that there's gonna be no official detour through our neighborhood, we're certainly going to get people who want to cut through," said Krans.
Peter Schmidt, a member of the commission, said he "conferred with city authorities" and his "understanding is there's no intention of diverting the traffic off of that street through Renaud or anywhere else."
City engineer explains traffic plans Semprini confirmed no detours through the neighborhood are planned.
"A temporary traffic control plan will be developed by the selected contractor before construction begins," she wrote to Foster's. "At this time, we anticipate construction operations will utilize lane closures, with one lane maintained for alternating two-way traffic controlled by flaggers. We do not currently anticipate implementing an official detour through surrounding neighborhood streets. Once a contractor is selected, the city will hold another public meeting to review the construction schedule, traffic control measures, and project sequencing. This meeting will provide residents with an opportunity to ask questions and provide input before construction begins."
She said Jenness Street is expected to be open during most of the project, except during some catch basin work.
Semprini said for the local traffic signage is not planned and is not enforceable, adding "our fear is that it would actually encourage people to use those neighborhoods if you put that signage up. So I would like to start the project without those signage and then evaluate if they're needed."
She also noted apps like Google Maps or Waze will "send vehicles the shortest distance and that's not something that the city can manage or fix."
This article originally appeared on Fosters Daily Democrat: Dover lower Central Ave. reconstruction raises traffic concerns
